India's government is a giant shopper.
From pens to bridges, five lakh crore rupees went through one government website last year.
So how do businesses actually win these orders?
Small buys? Officials can order directly.
Big ones become a tender. A public notice that anyone can bid on.
One proves you can do the job.
Pass round one, and your price gets opened.
The lowest price wins. It's called L one.
So where does the bribe come in?
Knowing your rival's price is gold.
The CBI has accused railway officials of leaking bid rates for cash.
In March, it says it caught a senior engineer accepting ten lakh rupees. The alleged ask? One percent of a forty crore tender.
Other times, companies secretly decide who wins.
Regulators caught railway suppliers sending rival bids from the same internet address.
That's why tenders moved online, where every click leaves a trail.
Fair on paper. But humans still run it.
